name: 29979-mintokensdecode-qwen332b-4gpu
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3, four GPUs of one a3 node.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=64, bounded at 1024 requests / 2400 s safety, first 10% warmup by completion (~922 requests scored). A 10% cooldown is also declared and does not fire: a percent phase anchors on the 2400 s safety cap, so its window opens long after the run has ended.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets: prompt exactly 300 tokens, output exactly 300, `ignore_eos` on, `request_format: plain`. Per-request sampling is declared in `scenario.json` and nowhere else: temperature 0.6, top_k 20, top_p 0.95, and min_tokens 300, which asks the engine for a reply of at least 300 tokens. Prompts are Faker-generated synthetic English.
purpose: A 32-billion-parameter chat assistant giving fixed-length 300-token replies to 64 concurrent users on four GPUs.
launch:
# vLLM at commit 3a7751485b71ce5ef927e4aa03b28602cb90811c. The interpreter and the hardware seal
# are in configs/env.yaml, which is this machine's and is not portable.

model: Qwen/Qwen3-32B
tensor-parallel-size: 4

# 2048 clears the workload's 300-in / 300-out worst case. Left unset, the engine takes the
# checkpoint's 40960 and sizes the KV pool for a window nothing here uses.
max-model-len: 2048

# The values a `vllm serve` resolves to on >=70 GiB non-A100 cards at this commit, written down so
# that a later change of default cannot move the operating point.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 256
enable-chunked-prefill: true

# Off: every prompt is 300 freshly sampled synthetic tokens with no configured shared prefix, so a
# cache could never hit, and turning it off removes the block-hashing work with it.
enable-prefix-caching: false

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
